A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scaling-law study. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack experiments on image classifiers, multimodal models and adversarially trained models, including appendix results and visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional defense, untargeted-attack, optimizer-comparison and curve-fitting analyses.

M1.justification: The targeted SSA-CWA procedure and CLIP embedding objective remain. v2 Section 5.1 adds an untargeted adaptation that maximizes loss for the natural class rather than minimizing target-class loss. The new pseudocode documents the existing SSA-CWA combination.

E1.justification: v2 adds directly optimized untargeted attacks and input-purification scenarios involving HGD, BDR, JPEG and DiffPure. v1's untargeted defense metric instead scored examples generated through targeted attacks. NIPS17 and multimodal-model coverage remain unchanged after matching v1's appendix results.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 7b adds evaluated VMI-CWA and MI-SVRE comparisons alongside MI-CWA and MI-FGSM. v1 already compared CWA with MI-FGSM gradients and MI-CWA with SSA-CWA success rates; those comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The reported 64-model surrogate pool replaces two adversarially trained Inception models with Twins-SVT and NFNet, and a ViT training description changes. The nine-model RobustBench defense evaluation is replaced by six defenses. New protocols use epsilon 2/255 for untargeted attacks and a cat-target optimizer comparison averaged across target models. These reported changes do not establish rerunning of retained results.

E4.justification: v2 adds optimizer-dependence and untargeted-scaling analyses in Figure 7 and fitting-error diagnostics in Table 3. Its six-defense analysis replaces v1's nine-model robustness analysis. v1's normal-versus-adversarially-trained saliency comparison is removed; perturbation and image-generation visualizations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or sampling-uncertainty estimates. v2's new MSE table measures residual fitting error for existing curves, rather than uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: v1's flat defense-scaling results disappear, while v2 reports increasing ASR on a different defense suite, new Figure 7 results and ASR fitting MSEs of 0.0023–0.0040. Phi-3-vision and DeepSeek-VL curve assignments are swapped between v1 Figure 4 and v2 Figure 5. All 90 multimodal scores from v1 Tables 2 and 6 are retained in v2 Table 2. The replacement defense results are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 11 adds a formal untargeted maximization problem. Definitions 1–2, both convergence theorems, their assumptions and rates, and the Appendix A proof otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion explicitly claim generality across defenses and attack algorithms. This broadens v1's scope, whose introduction highlighted failure on adversarially trained models. The introduction also raises the headline success claim for other commercial MLLMs from over 60% to over 80%, although the corresponding tabulated scores are retained.

C2.justification: v1 Section 6.2 and Appendix F explain defense failures through different feature distributions and restrict scaling accordingly. v2 removes that limitation and explanation, asserts applicability across defenses, and adds an optimizer-dependent explanation involving gradient conflicts and variance reduction. The theoretical i.i.d. caveat and ASR-saturation qualification remain.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix C adds SSA-CWA pseudocode specifying spectrum averaging, sequential surrogate updates, inner and outer momentum, and clipping. Figure 2 also newly identifies random inputs from the experimental dataset. These additions improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained algorithm.

R1.justification: v2 adds a discussion connecting attack scaling to Wei et al.'s in-context jailbreaking work, associated language-model security citations, and references for newly evaluated defenses. Several references supporting the removed robustness study disappear. The principal positioning against earlier small-ensemble research remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, related work moves from Section 2 to Appendix G, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around defended models and generality. The former Further Studies section becomes Discussions with new subsections, alongside terminology and language revisions.

P2.justification: v2 merges v1's main and appendix multimodal tables, adds defense and ablation plots, a fitting-error table and an algorithm display, and removes the earlier defense plot and saliency panel. Retained figures are resized or relocated, ASR table headings are corrected, and the open-model plot's legend assignments change.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful optimizer and untargeted tests, fitting diagnostics and pseudocode, and aligns the open-model legend with the retained discussion. However, it removes v1's nine-model RobustBench counterexamples and replaces them with a different defense suite while claiming universality, without reconciling the earlier negative evidence. The documentation and analytical gains coexist with a loss of demonstrated applicability limits, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
